translations.text: Let this be known to all of you who read or copy this holy book, O saints of God: that this blessed father,
who composed this soul-illuminating book, is not called Climacus, God forbid, but his name is John;
rather it is the book that is called Climax, and in the Greek language Climax means "Ladder."
And this book is called Ladder for this reason: because he made this book like a ladder of virtues, and it begins from lowly deeds,
and chapter by chapter it ascends to the lofty ones, as you will find the Ladder of Virtues depicted at the very end of the book.
But the one who earlier translated that small selection had called that saint Climacus. Now then, if anyone speaks the name of the book, let him say Climax, which is Ladder;
but if he speaks the name of that saint, let him say John. Since, indeed, in that first translation many things had been written crookedly and many had been left out,
therefore I, the poor Euthymius, by the command of my holy father John, have translated this just as that saint himself said it in Greek, for he was Greek by birth.
Now therefore, you who read this holy book, make prayer for our holy fathers, for John and for John Synkellos, and also for me, the sinner Euthymius,
and you who copy it, write it just as you find it here.
And set down the chapter headings as they are here, for I too have set them down as I found them, all in red;
and let none of you omit these words either, but write them, for God's sake, along with my sinful name as well.
